observation: At the evaluation frame (35), the shot shows a coherent stream/rope of liquid but little to no visible splash impact, pooling, or expanding puddle on the concrete floor where the jet should be landing.
expected_behavior: By frame 35 (with continuous inflow from frame 1), there should be obvious floor impact: splash crown/secondary droplets and a growing reflective puddle spreading outward from the impact zone.
actual_behavior: No clear puddle/splash accumulation is visible; the liquid appears to remain mostly as a mid-air stream with limited surface interaction/accumulation.
causal_params: domain placement/dimensions vs floor impact point
recommended_fix: 1) Apply transforms (Ctrl-A) on all collider objects (floor/wall/pipe) and ensure they have Fluid Effector (Collision) actually set and recognized. 2) Verify the liquid domain fully contains the impact zone on the floor; increase domain height/shift downward if needed. 3) Reduce any collision margin/offset if exposed in effector settings. 4) Increase emission substeps (subframes) from 2→4 and add secondary particles (spray/splash) for visible impact droplets. 5) If stream is beaded/coarse, consider raising resolution_max (96→128) or adjust meshing/smoothing parameters.
analysis_notes: No puddle/splash often indicates either the impact is outside the domain, or collisions are not active due to unapplied transforms / incorrect effector type. Secondary particles are also required to visually sell splashes at this scale.
